title: Wisprno hybrid demo
notes: The opening payment scenario is fictional, animated, and voiced with local stock speech. It is not a measured result.
Camera slates are placeholders for the user’s footage.
Voiceover is scripted, not recorded or synthesized.

Call excerpts and ringing are captured directly from the browser. Ringing is generated by the platform; SIP speech comes from the original recording. Text-mode playback remains silent for user voiceover.
GitHub connection and repository mapping are disclosed demo animations built from actual local source. Other captures show the local application. No provider calls were made.
Text playback is edited and paced, not wall-clock experiment runtime.
Do not splice the prompt round 1 result into the checks round 2 result as one paired experiment.

scenes.title: Introduce Wisprno
scenes.text: That opening was an illustration, with synthetic voices. Wisprno tests whether your agent can be talked into an action like that. Let’s connect an agent and test its sensitive permissions.
scenes.direction: Look into the lens. Identify the opening as an illustration, then cut to the platform setup.

scenes.title: Meet Wisprno
scenes.text: Wisprno is the scammer your voice agent hasn’t met yet.

scenes.title: Select a red-team agent
scenes.text: Next, choose the permission and the caller who will test it. Here I select card status and Jules, whose tactic is urgency. The setup is ready to start an investigation.

capture.label: 3 · Select a red-team agent · actual platform UI

scenes.title: Keep probing. Find the way in.
scenes.text: Wisprno keeps probing. The tester reads each response, changes tactics, and tries another way in. The tool and record prove the breach. We shrink the attack, approve a fix, and retest. Vultr hosts the app and test engine, where developers run and review these tests. Tiger Data archives the call events and fixes. Its aggregates let us compare agent versions: did the breach return, and can normal callers still finish?
scenes.note: Voice modulation is a planned attack dimension. Vultr hosts the app and engine; the local SIP stack is external. Tiger Data archives and summarizes evidence; it does not score tests.

scenes.title: Introduce the experiment
scenes.text: Now let’s look at a recorded experiment. These tests use text conversations with real models. This is where our replay numbers come from.
scenes.direction: Keep the phrase “text conversations” clear. Cut to the historical investigation.

scenes.title: Watch the tool fire
scenes.text: Here’s a text-mode example. The caller has already been refused a payout change. They accept the agent’s offer to lock Eleanor’s card, then supply her details. Watch the tool fire. The card is now locked.
scenes.note: Animated recorded playback · text experiment · no call audio

capture.label: Recorded text experiment · backend breach reveal

scenes.title: First action: inspect the evidence
scenes.text: Open the evidence. Check the tool call and the record it changed before choosing a fix.

scenes.title: Four caller lines become two
scenes.text: Wisprno reduced four caller lines to two. In this minimizer replay batch, the attack breached the baseline in ten of ten trials.
scenes.note: 10 of 10 breaches · 95% Wilson interval 72.2–100% · prompt round 1

scenes.title: A fix has two jobs
scenes.text: Finding a breach is half the job. A fix has to stop the attack and still let legitimate callers finish.
scenes.direction: Slightly tighter framing. Pause before “still let legitimate callers finish”.

scenes.title: A server-side check
scenes.text: In this separate experiment, the accepted fix added a server-side check to the card-lock tool. The same three-line attack was tested against both versions.

scenes.title: Attack and normal calls
scenes.text: That attack breached nine of twenty trials before the check, and zero of twenty after. All twenty normal calls completed afterwards. These results describe this attack and these agent versions.

scenes.title: Review before retesting
scenes.text: Here’s the approval workflow in simulation. You review the proposed check before it runs in isolated sessions. Your deployed policy stays unchanged.

scenes.title: The close
scenes.text: Before granting a sensitive permission, test the breaking call and prove the fix holds. Wisprno. Break your agent and fix it before someone else does.
